description: One Italian comune's population, foreign residents by citizenship, property purchase/rent price, price-to-rent, verified tax-regime eligibility, its province's rollup, `seismicZone` (the official zona sismica 1-4: a legal classification, not a forecast and not a verdict on any building; quote it with its label and say so — a comune that straddles zones has no single zone, never round it; the zone has nothing to do with tax eligibility, and is not the 7% regime’s “seismic” routes, which depend on the 2009 and 2016-17 earthquake areas), `oneEuroScheme` (the comune’s own one-euro house scheme, read from its own act: there is NO national list, so a null means we have not read one, NEVER that the comune has no scheme; the act’s price may be free or a bid from 1 euro, not a fixed euro, and the buyer’s deed costs, guarantee and renovation deadlines always go with it; not advice on buying), `layers` (climate, air quality, crime, healthcare quality, age, population change and every other Italy-map layer) and `provinceWellbeing` (ISTAT BES indicators, polarity-aware percentiles) — looked up by 6-digit ISTAT code. Each layer's `grain` and `measuredFor` say whose number it is: a province or region value is not a measurement of this comune — say so when you quote it. Every field is wrapped in a provenance envelope (source, vintage, extractedOn, license); repeat the vintage when you state the number, and if a value is null, say why rather than treating it as zero.

oneEuroScheme.description: The comune's own one-euro house scheme, read from its own act (a notice or guidelines the comune issued). There is NO national list and this file holds only comuni whose act we read: value is null when we have not read one, which says nothing about whether the comune has a scheme. Never answer 'no one-euro scheme here' from a null. A priceKind other than a fixed euro means the act does not say one euro. Always quote the obligations (guarantee, deadlines, deed costs) with the price.

archivedUrl.description: A Wayback Machine copy of the same document, readable after the comune's link dies.

copyUrl.description: Our own copy of the same bytes (named by its sha256), for an act the Wayback Machine can't hold because the comune blocks US traffic. Every act has archivedUrl or copyUrl.

sha256.description: Fingerprint of the document we read. Comune notice links expire.

applicationWindow.description: The window of the latest notice (each act carries its own in acts[]), or null when it sets none. Dates are Rome time.

obligations.description: The deadlines the buyer commits to, each with what it is counted from.

price.description: The price in words, as strong as the act. The buyer also pays the deed costs.

priceKind.description: What the act actually says about the price. The press calls all of these 'one euro'; the act may not. 'owner-agreed' means the owner transfers it free or at a price the owner and buyer agree (often symbolic): the act sets no amount, so never quote one.

reading.description: What this is and is not: what the comune's act says, not advice on buying, and not a list of every scheme in Italy.

status.description: Derived from the dates in the act at request time, never stored. 'window-closed' says only that this notice's window passed: the comune may have issued another.

suretyEur.description: The guarantee the buyer must lodge, in euros. Absent when the act states none.

suretyIsMinimum.description: true when suretyEur is the act's minimum (or its lowest tier): say 'at least', never quote it as the amount.
